evals.prompt: I just exported our January and February payroll results from SAP. Can you compare them and tell me what changed? The files are payroll_current.xlsx and payroll_prior.xlsx
evals.expected_output: A variance analysis report showing period-over-period changes by wage type, cost center, and employee, with natural language explanations for significant variances
expectations: The output identifies the total payroll amount for both periods
The output calculates the overall variance (dollar and percentage)
The output breaks down variances by wage type category (1000=Basic Pay, 1100=OT, 2001=FIT, etc.)
The output flags variances exceeding the default tolerance threshold (5% AND $500)
The output detects 2 new hires (00044701, 00044715) appearing only in current period
The output detects 2 terminated employees (00044801, 00044815) appearing only in prior period
The output identifies the salary increases for Charles Brown (00043156, 5%) and George Lee (00043302, 3%)
The output notes the medical plan change for Julia Thomas (00043425)
The output provides natural language explanations for significant variances
An XLSX variance report file is generated with multiple sheets

evals.prompt: Our CFO is asking why labor costs jumped in cost center 4500 this month. I have the payroll exports - can you dig into what's driving the increase and give me something I can send to her?
evals.expected_output: A focused analysis of cost center 4500 variances with an executive-ready summary document
expectations: The analysis specifically addresses cost center 4500
The output identifies overtime as a major driver (higher OT factor in current period)
The output lists the specific employees in CC 4500 and their individual variances
An executive-ready summary is produced (either DOCX or well-formatted text)
The output includes dollar amounts and percentages
The language is appropriate for CFO-level communication

evals.prompt: compare these two payroll runs and flag anything over 10% change or more than $1000 difference. i need to review before we release production payroll tomorrow
evals.expected_output: A filtered variance analysis using custom thresholds (10% / $1000) with urgency-appropriate formatting
expectations: The analysis uses 10% as the percentage threshold
The analysis uses $1000 as the absolute threshold
Only variances exceeding BOTH thresholds are flagged (AND logic for pre-production)
The output is organized for quick pre-production review
The tone reflects the urgency of a pre-production check
New hires and terminated employees are flagged as anomalies requiring sign-off
